name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
summary: Hospitalisation cover for people who meet the applicable beneficiary criteria. The 70+ expansion is a separate route; verify and enrol through the official beneficiary service.
benefit: Up to ₹5 lakh per eligible family per year under the national scheme. The 70+ expansion was announced irrespective of income; card creation and beneficiary verification still apply. State implementation and interactions with other public schemes can vary.
criteria: General PM-JAY beneficiary status is determined through the official beneficiary identification process and applicable State/UT rules.
People aged 70 and above can check the Ayushman Vay Vandana route irrespective of income.
ASHA workers, Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi Helpers and their families were included through a separate expansion; official verification is required.
documents: The official beneficiary portal explains the current verification and enrolment requirements. Do not submit identity documents to EpidemAI.

actions.label: Check or verify on the official beneficiary portal

source_label: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare / PIB

name: Delhi Arogya Nidhi
summary: Delhi financial assistance for qualifying patients receiving treatment at government hospitals. The official scheme record lists a National Food Security Card and Delhi residence criteria.
benefit: Financial assistance up to ₹1.5 lakh is described on the official myScheme record. Amounts and terms must be confirmed with the Delhi authority before relying on them.
criteria: The myScheme record lists a National Food Security Card.
It lists at least three years of continuous Delhi residence before application.
Treatment must be at a government hospital in Delhi.
The final decision and required documents are confirmed by the responsible Delhi authority.
documents: Government hospital estimate and treatment records; see the official scheme page for the current list.

actions.label: Review details and verify with Delhi

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
summary: A maternity programme that provides cash assistance for eligible institutional deliveries. Criteria and amounts depend on state category and other scheme conditions.
benefit: Cash assistance may be available for eligible institutional delivery; the applicable amount and conditions must be checked with the State Health Mission or official scheme office.
criteria: Pregnancy alone does not confirm JSY cash eligibility.
NHM criteria differ between low-performing and high-performing states and depend on facility and beneficiary category.
Check the current state rules and official enrolment process.
documents: Ask the local ASHA/health facility or State Health Mission for the current document list.

name: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
jurisdiction: Central; delivered through public health institutions
summary: Public-facility entitlements for delivery-related care and eligible sick newborns/infants. Ask the public facility or ASHA how the service is provided locally.
benefit: NHM describes free delivery including C-section, medicines and consumables, diagnostics, blood when needed, diet, exemption from user charges and transport. Similar entitlements extend to sick newborns and infants up to one year, subject to programme conditions.
criteria: Pregnant women delivering in public health institutions are covered by the described entitlements.
Similar provisions apply to sick newborns and infants accessing public institutions; confirm the current local process.
documents: Ask the public facility or ASHA about local registration and records to bring.

name: Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)
summary: Government immunisation information for eligible children and pregnant women. It is a public-health programme, not an insurance scheme or means-tested benefit.
benefit: MoHFW describes vaccines provided through UIP for eligible beneficiaries. Follow the current official schedule and confirm a local session with the health facility.
criteria: Vaccination schedule depends on age, pregnancy and prior doses; a healthcare worker can review the individual schedule.
documents: Bring any available vaccination card or record to the public facility; ask the facility about local requirements.
source_label: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

name: Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM)
summary: Community-level comprehensive primary healthcare. Programme design includes preventive and primary care; a specific centre's services and hours must be confirmed locally.
benefit: The official portal describes a range of primary healthcare services, including maternal and child health, screening, essential medicines and diagnostics. This is not a personal insurance or cash-benefit determination.
criteria: Use public service information without scheme eligibility screening.
Confirm exact service, hours and availability with the centre.
documents: No scheme documents are required to browse this information. Ask the centre about any visit-specific records.

actions.label: Open official Ayushman Arogya Mandir portal
Search nearby centres on a map

source_label: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)
summary: Participating Janaushadhi Kendras provide generic medicines at lower prices. This is not a promise that a particular medicine is free or in stock.
benefit: The official PMBI site describes affordable generic medicines through dedicated outlets. Check the current product price and stock with the Kendra; do not change a prescription without a clinician or pharmacist.
criteria: No personal eligibility match is needed to browse the programme.
Product availability and price vary; confirm with the outlet.
documents: No scheme documents are required to browse programme information.
source_label: Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India

name: National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)
jurisdiction: Central; public and identified treatment centres
summary: TB-specific public diagnostic and treatment services. This is listed as a general public programme, not as a diagnosis or suggestion that a person has TB.
benefit: The Central TB Division describes free diagnostic and treatment services through public health services. Confirm the service and location with an official TB centre.
criteria: A healthcare professional determines whether TB evaluation is relevant.
The navigator does not use symptoms to identify or diagnose TB.
documents: Ask the health facility about records needed for a visit.

name: ABHA — Ayushman Bharat Health Account
summary: A digital health account intended to support access to and consent-based sharing of health records in the ABDM ecosystem. It is not medical-cost coverage or insurance.
benefit: Use the official portal to learn about creating and managing an ABHA account. EpidemAI does not ask for an ABHA number and does not link records to this prototype.
criteria: Optional digital-health service; it is not required to use the Individual Health Portal.
documents: Any identity verification, if needed, must happen only on the official ABHA destination.

actions.label: Review ABHA on the National Portal of India

name: Delhi PM-JAY state top-up
summary: Delhi announced an additional ₹5 lakh annual family cover for eligible PM-JAY beneficiary families. Check current State Health Agency rules and beneficiary status before relying on the top-up.
benefit: The cited Government of India announcement describes ₹5 lakh in additional annual cover for eligible families under Delhi implementation. This is not a separate benefit for every Delhi resident.
criteria: A person must meet PM-JAY beneficiary requirements and the current Delhi implementation rules.
The announcement is not an individual eligibility confirmation; verify with the official beneficiary service and Delhi State Health Agency.
documents: Use the official beneficiary service for eligibility and enrollment requirements; do not submit identity documents to EpidemAI.
source_label: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

name: Delhi Government Employees Health Scheme (DGEHS)
summary: A medical-benefit scheme for eligible serving Delhi government employees, pensioners and eligible family members. It is separate from PM-JAY and ABHA.
benefit: The Delhi Directorate General of Health Services describes outpatient care, investigations and treatment through recognized government facilities and notified empanelled providers, subject to current scheme rules and membership.
criteria: The official scheme page lists serving GNCTD employees and pensioners (including eligible family members) as beneficiary groups.
Membership, contribution, referral and provider rules depend on current DGEHS terms; check the official portal.
documents: Check current membership, contribution and claim documents on the official DGEHS site.

actions.label: Review DGEHS rules and provider information

source_label: Directorate General of Health Services, Government of NCT of Delhi

name: Uttar Pradesh National Health Mission information
summary: The Uttar Pradesh NHM portal is a starting point for state health-programme information, notices and service updates. It is not a single cash benefit or an eligibility determination.
benefit: Programme-specific services and beneficiary criteria differ. Use the UP NHM and Health Department portals to find current details, local contacts and application routes.
criteria: State programmes may depend on residence, life stage, beneficiary category or facility.
This portal record does not assert eligibility for any individual scheme.
documents: Check the linked official state portal for programme-specific requirements.

actions.label: Open Uttar Pradesh National Health Mission

name: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)
summary: A public child-health screening and early-intervention programme. Ask a public health facility or local health worker how screening is arranged in your area.
benefit: The official RBSK portal provides programme information. Screening scope, age groups, referral and local service availability should be confirmed with the health system.
criteria: This is child-focused public-health information, not a cash benefit or diagnosis.
The navigator does not use symptoms to determine whether a child has a condition.
documents: Ask the local public health facility about the applicable screening and referral process.
source_label: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, RBSK Portal
